To: ashbourne-terrace-chimney
Replying to: p05
Cc: none
Subject: DRAFT — Please do not enter 43 or attempt propping

Mick, please don’t go into 43 at 9, with your lad or otherwise. Priya, please don’t hand over a key for this. That includes going inside to inspect the loft.

I’m a chartered structural engineer with IStructE, but I’m writing as a neighbour who looked from the opposite pavement at about 7. This is not a commissioned inspection or professional assessment, and I have no PI cover for informal advice. I cannot certify either house or the pavement as safe.

What I could see was concerning: about 1.2 metres of chimney remains at 41, leaning towards 43, with visibly deteriorated mortar at its base. There is a substantial hole in 43’s roof, a stepped crack above the bay and apparent movement at the bay head. Loose slates along the gutter line at 43 and 45 are directly above the footway.

Under that holed roof, with the remaining stack above, is precisely where nobody should be standing. Floors may already be carrying fallen masonry; we don’t know what is supporting what now. Putting in props without that assessment could make matters worse.

Jo’s cousin is right that terraces can be robust generally. This one is damaged; that general reassurance cannot establish its safety.

Please use the other side of the road, especially on the school run. The tape covers only 43’s front garden, not the pavement. The council already knows, but needs an urgent update about the overhead debris and unclosed footway. Dangerous structures out of hours is reached through the main council number. If anything starts falling or anyone is in immediate danger, call 999.

Priya, 45 looked undamaged from the front, but I could not see the shared wall. Mrs Doherty’s decision isn’t mine, but I would not sleep in her front room tonight. Staying with family until 45 has been checked would be the safer precaution.

To: dm:Gary_41

Subject: DRAFT — Chimney information

Gary, I won’t put your private message on the forum. Please tell the council’s dangerous structures officer about the removed chimney breasts and reported brackets straight away: they need that information before anyone enters or plans support. Please don’t go inside to check them yourself.

That information alone does not establish why the chimney fell, and I can’t judge insurance cover. We can talk privately, but please don’t delay telling the officer while waiting for me.
